post.description:
Batched menu OCR for the field pipeline.

All (<=6) menu photos go to the primary model in a single multimodal
request (the OpenRouter model in ``OUTREACH_OCR_MODEL``). If the structural
confidence is <70% or nothing is parsed, a single fallback request goes to
the direct OpenAI API (``gpt-4o-mini``) with Pillow-deskewed/contrast
images. A global budget (default 45s, env-tunable) bounds the whole
orchestration; on exhaustion
or double failure we return ``ocr_failed`` so the agent can type the menu.

Every attempt is tagged with an ``attempt_id`` and logged/recorded with a
``category`` so backend devs can tell an IMAGE fault (bad/unreadable photo ->
retake) from a PROCESSING fault (provider/timeout -> retry).

get.description:
Progress for a chunked menu OCR job (>6 pages). The wizard polls this
after a 202 from menu-ocr.

Settlement + reconciliation report for the dispatcher console.

Aggregates orders created in the window (EAT days), realized restaurant and
driver payouts, refunds, payment-rail mix, per-driver performance, COD
custody, and a daily series for the range.

Factual operational report for the console (EAT window).

Every figure is computed from stored records: order timestamps, the eta
window captured at checkout (`eta_min`/`eta_max`), cancellation reason
codes, COD ledger rows, restaurant-bill timestamps, arrival-SLA breaches,
dispatch assignment events and customer ratings. Metrics whose inputs were
never captured are returned as null with an entry in `capture_gaps` — the
UI must render them as "not captured", never as zero or an estimate.

Paginated hold detail with per-row order linkage (additive).

Rows carry the canonical order_id when the reservation has one; records
without a linkage are returned with order_id "" and order_link "unknown"
(never silently dropped, never auto-reconciled). Aggregates stay on the
existing ledger endpoint; totals here match the returned filter scope.

Ledger-derived money view for the dispatch console.

The wallet value already moves with real operations (restaurant payments
debit it via `$inc`), so instead of a bare editable number the console gets
the breakdown: recorded balance, live holds, realized payouts/refunds and
COD cash in courier custody.

Scoped queue with search, filters, stable pagination and lane counts.

`status` accepts up to 24 comma-separated values (raised from 12: the
console's lifecycle list has 18 statuses and the old cap silently dropped
the late-lifecycle ones).

Additive: callers with no params keep the previous behaviour (same 250-row
first page of non-terminal orders, oldest first). `counts` reflects the
search/filters WITHOUT the status filter so lane badges stay accurate while
a lane is open; `total` is the count for the full filter set. Search is
entity-resolved (order id / short code / restaurant name / customer phone)
so every branch uses an indexed field — no unbounded scans.

Read-only audit trail for one order: lifecycle events, the float
reservation, float ledger events and the COD ledger row. No mutations.
Operator quick templates with their addressed audience (read-only).

Open (optionally resolved) payment-authorization alerts — alert-only;
no reservation is released and no money moves from this endpoint.

post.description:
Resume a transfer-verified order after the operator refills the float.

This does not accept another payment reference or credit the wallet again.

get.description: Paginated completed/cancelled deliveries for the driver dashboard.
Driver earnings: today / last 7 days / lifetime + payout + COD status.

Per-order COD ledger rows for the custody workspace (additive read).

Complements `/ops/cod-outstanding` (per-driver totals) so the console can
show exactly which orders make up a driver's balance before a handover.

Real courier roster for the console (additive read).

Only recorded fields are returned: account status, vehicle, KYC state,
active assignment, deliveries/unpaid fees in the window, arrival-SLA
breaches, gate no-show resolutions, customer ratings and current COD
balance. No GPS positions, no estimates.

post.description:
CSV candidate import: name,latitude,longitude,category,source,phone,notes.

Candidates are stored ``unverified`` and never treated as verified outlets.

Stamp `restaurant_id` on field outlets that already have a matching row in
the shared `restaurants` table (matched by `outlet_id`).

Read-only on `restaurants`; writes only the agreed link field on our own
`field_outlets` docs. This is the DB-only bridge — no cross-lane HTTP.

get.description:
One atomic, immutable day package for the field app's offline cache.

Each route also carries a full ``RouteDetail``-shaped record under
``details`` so the client can cache and drop it straight into the route
screen without reassembling it.

post.description:
Produce a next-day assignment plan using the spec rules.

Deterministic. Prioritizes incomplete/exception-heavy neighborhoods, two
teams per neighborhood on separate sectors, skips already-completed routes,
and records every active team either a route or an explicit no_route.

get.description:
Latest accepted GPS fix per crew route for the Field Ops Live Map.

One fix per crew (the newest accepted breadcrumb), with a staleness flag so
a manager can tell at a glance which crews are walking and which have gone
quiet. No raw point dumps — one fix per route.
Grouped, printable route cards per crew for a date.

The caller's routes.

Defaults to OPEN work: every route for the caller's crew that is not yet
terminal (``approved_complete``/``cancelled``) regardless of planned date,
so unfinished routes carry over day to day instead of disappearing at
midnight. Pass ``route_date`` for a strict single-day listing.

post.description:
Manager closes out an exception so the segment counts against coverage again.

Resolving is the missing half of the loop: previously an exception was
permanent, so `completion_gaps` exempted its segment forever and a
blocked/unsafe route could never recover.

Compress and privately store field evidence.

The outlet may be identified by server ``outlet_id`` (online capture) or by
``outlet_client_op_id`` (a capture queued offline before the outlet synced).
Repeated client op ids return the already-created record.
